claims.text: Long-range chemical ordering governs phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Al atoms drive formation of ordered B2 relative to a disordered FCC solid solution.
Long-range ordering governs retention of high-temperature strength.
Long-range ordering governs retention of environmental resistance.
Long-range ordering governs retention of radiation tolerance.
Long-range ordering governs retention of cryogenic toughness.
The proposed baseline can be processed into a homogeneous disordered FCC structure with minimal short- or long-range ordering.
A slight increase in Al concentration promotes long-range chemical ordering.
Controlled annealing can nucleate an ordered B2 phase.
The ordered B2 phase can coexist with or replace portions of the disordered FCC matrix.
Controlled ordering increases bond-energy differences among the constituent elements.
Increased bond-energy differences stabilize the phase by reducing the driving force for phase separation.
Ordering enhances high-temperature strength by impeding dislocation motion.
Ordering enhances radiation tolerance by limiting defect mobility.
Ordering maintains or improves cryogenic toughness by dampening transformation-induced damage.
The ordered variant will resist phase decomposition during thermal cycling better than the disordered baseline.
The ordered variant will have greater high-temperature strength than the disordered baseline.
The ordered variant will have better radiation-damage resistance than the disordered baseline.
The ordered variant will maintain or improve cryogenic toughness relative to the disordered baseline.
The proposed mechanism ceases to operate at sufficiently high temperatures that cause disorder or at sufficiently low Al contents.

contradictions.description: The comparison is said to vary only the degree of atomic ordering, but the proposed intervention changes Al concentration and applies an annealing treatment absent from the baseline. Composition and thermal history are therefore additional variables.
The conditions require only ordering to vary, whereas the mediator permits B2 to coexist with or replace FCC, which also varies phase constitution and phase fraction rather than ordering alone.
